A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same conditional-score transformation framework, renamed from SDPS to UCoS. The main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A-E are readable and matchable despite retitling and reformatting.

before.justification: v2 reports original LIDC-IRI CT reconstruction experiments, posterior-sample statistics, sampling times, and FNO capacity studies in Section 5 and Appendix E.

after.justification: v3 reports updated CT experiments and original CelebA deblurring results, including numerical comparisons and posterior samples in Section 5 and Appendix E.

M1.justification: The FNO input transformation changes from multiplication by min(exp(t)-1,1) in v2 Figure 3 to x/(1+std(x)) in v3 Figure 4. This changes a model component, while the conditional-score identity, training objective, and overall sampling framework remain. Renaming SDPS to UCoS and expanding implementation explanations do not themselves establish additional method changes.

E1.justification: v2 evaluates CT reconstruction using LIDC-IRI. v3 retains that coverage and adds Gaussian-convolution deblurring using CelebA face images, introducing both a different image domain and a distinct inverse task.

E2.justification: The CT comparisons retain SDE ALD, DPS, Proj, and Conditional, including the appendix comparisons at different FNO widths. v3 extends the same comparator set to deblurring. Newly discussed related methods are not added to the empirical comparisons.

E3.justification: The reported FNO input normalization changes, and the capacity sweep drops its highest-width plotted setting. The new deblurring experiment uses 175-by-175 images and 1,000 posterior samples, except 100 for Proj, whose implementation uses a very small batch size. Existing CT geometry, noise level, training budgets, and 1,000-step sampling protocol remain stated as before.

E4.justification: The existing sensitivity study of FNO width and image resolution is revised: v2 Figures 2/9 become v3 Figures 3/11 with changed bias and standard-deviation curves and a reduced width range. The underlying question remains the same. Spatial bias/std maps already appear in v2; their clearer captions in v3 do not constitute a new analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions report posterior-ensemble standard deviations and spatial uncertainty maps. v3 applies the same reporting practice to deblurring and adds no independent training-run or seed information, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Changed posterior sample counts concern the evaluation protocol.

E6.justification: CT statistics change across all three reported FNO widths and the scaling plots. For example, Table 1 changes SDPS/UCoS bias, std, and time from 0.0477, 0.0319, and 24 minutes to 0.0498, 0.0316, and 27 minutes. v3 also adds deblurring results, including UCoS bias 0.0884 and std 0.0345 in Table 2. These are revised or additional results; the input-normalization change prevents treating them as controlled same-procedure performance gains.

T1.justification: Section 3.3.1 adds a derivation of the transformed training-input covariance and its Gaussian sampling representation. The main theorems and Appendix A-C arguments are retained. The new online-score formula in Section 3.3.2 subtracts exp(-t/2)x, introducing an inconsistency with the retained Equation 15, which requires exp(t/2)x.

C1.justification: v3 explicitly claims a fully matrix-free implementation requiring forward-operator and adjoint access, particularly in Section 1.1. This extends the stated computational property beyond avoiding forward evaluations during online sampling. The central exact-score identity, convergence guarantee, and infinite-dimensional formulation claims remain.

C2.justification: The conclusion newly explains that the exact transformation relies on a linear forward model and Gaussian likelihood through completing the square. It explicitly identifies nonlinear and non-Gaussian extensions as nontrivial future work. v2 discusses alternative diffusion processes but lacks this substantive applicability qualification.

D1.justification: New Section 3.3 substantially expands implementation documentation by giving a direct Gaussian construction of training inputs, identifying required operator applications, and separating offline training from online sampling with a precomputed observation shift. Appendix D also revises input normalization, describes the deblurring Proj memory workaround, and changes the code pointer to a specific repository branch. Most existing hardware and training hyperparameters are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds references including Daras, Denker, Chen, and Yao, plus FNO and CelebA sources. Section 1.1 adds the Doob h-transform approach and expands the comparison with MCGDiff, positioning UCoS's matrix-free implementation against MCGDiff's stated SVD requirement. The broader related-work organization remains.

P1.justification: The title and abstract are rewritten, SDPS becomes UCoS throughout, Section 3 gains explicit theory/approximation/implementation subdivisions, and Section 5 separates CT, deblurring, and scaling discussions. The conclusion is expanded, but most existing exposition, the overall section order, and the appendix organization remain.

P2.justification: The two-column main text becomes a single-column document with a redesigned title/author block and extensively reflowed equations, tables, and figures. v3 adds deblurring Table 2 and Figures 2/10, redraws the scaling plots, and expands captions. Existing CT figures and the FNO diagram remain identifiable across renumbering and relocation.

improvement.justification: The deblurring experiment tests applicability beyond CT, while the explicit matrix-free training construction and linear/Gaussian limitation discussion address gaps in v2's practical explanation and scope. These provide a limited net quality improvement. The gains are tempered by the new sampling-formula inconsistency with Equation 15 and incomplete specification of the deblurring kernel and noise.
